India Bihar aims to link one crore women directly with jobs: CM Samrat Choudhary PTI 19 September, 2026 09:45 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 19 (PTI) Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday said the state government aims to directly link one crore women with employment, while expanding opportunities for their economic empowerment, higher education and safety. Addressing the 25th foundation day ceremony of the Bihar State Commission for Women here, Choudhary said women were playing an increasingly important role in the state’s economic, social and political life. He said programmes such as JEEViKA and Chief Minister’s Women Employment Scheme were providing women opportunities in tailoring, poultry farming, goat rearing and other economic activities. Show Full Article “The government’s target is to directly link one crore women with employment,” said the chief minister. Under the ‘Balika PhD Fellowship’ programme, 1,000 female students will receive Rs 10,000 per month every year to pursue higher education and research, he said, adding that the government was also working towards establishing a university dedicated to women. The chief minister said Bihar was the first state to introduce the ‘Police Didi’ initiative and deploy women police personnel around schools, colleges and other educational institutions for the safety of female students. Choudhary also released a special postage stamp on the Bihar State Commission for Women and unveiled its silver jubilee souvenir. He urged the Commission to go beyond grievance redressal and regularly advise the government on measures to improve women’s status. PTI PKD NN This report is auto-generated from PTI news service. bihar_raw_news.title: Congress to launch movement in Bihar over unorganised workers' rights - ThePrint
bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Congress to launch movement in Bihar over unorganised workers’ rights India Congress to launch movement in Bihar over unorganised workers’ rights PTI 19 September, 2026 07:46 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 19 (PTI) Senior Congress leader Udit Raj on Saturday said the party would launch a movement in Bihar to fight for the rights of workers in the unorganised sector, alleging that the new employment guarantee scheme had taken away the legal right to work guaranteed under MGNREGA. Addressing a press conference here, Raj said the biggest issue facing the country was that of labourers and unorganised-sector workers. The former MP alleged that though the VB-G RAM G scheme would provide 125 days of employment instead of the 100 days guaranteed under MGNREGA, the fundamental difference is that employment under the old scheme was a legal right, which had been removed under the new system. Show Full Article The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) is the country’s rural employment and development legislation enacted in December 2025 by the Centre. Its provisions came into force in Bihar from July 1 this year, replacing the older Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). “In a state like Bihar, where poverty and unemployment are serious problems, this will directly affect workers. The Congress party will launch a movement to fight for the rights of workers in the unorganised sector in Bihar,” Raj said. He, however, did not mention when the movement will be launched. Lack of adequate employment opportunities forces workers from the state to migrate to southern India, Punjab and other parts of the country, the Congress leader claimed. Democracy was being weakened, he alleged, asserting that protecting the Constitution was the responsibility of all citizens. “Bihar has given direction to several important movements for democracy and social justice. Congress workers in the state will have to further strengthen the struggle for democracy, the Constitution and social equality,” he said. Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee president Rajesh Ram said lakhs of workers employed in municipal corporations, government departments and various institutions faced issues related to wages, job security, social security, working conditions and labour rights. “The Congress has consistently raised its voice on these issues and will continue to do so,” he said. Ram said workers from SC, ST and other disadvantaged sections required special attention and should receive fair remuneration, dignity and their rights. bihar_raw_news.title: Tej Pratap Yadav intends to establish a 'darbaar' in the 'Rise & Fall 2' Penthouse - IANS LIVE
bihar_raw_news.content: Tej Pratap Yadav intends to establish a 'darbaar' in the 'Rise & Fall 2' Penthouse IANS September 19, 2026 3:04 PM Share on | Mumbai, Sep 19 (IANS) The son of veteran Bihar politician Lalu Prasad Yadav and a former Bihar minister, Tej Pratap Yadav, will be entering the unpredictable "Rise & Fall Season 2" Tower soon. Reflecting on the time when others may have celebrated seeing him shaken, the politician was seen invoking the might of a Bargad. Tej Pratap made a strong declaration of his strength in the clip, saying, "Jab hum udte samay dagmaya aur sab maje le rahe the par woh bhul gaye ke hum bargadh hai bargadh jiska daali se zyaada mazbood hai jadh aur issliye aa rahe hai Rise & Fall pe gardha udane. (“A lot of people enjoyed it when I wavered with flying; however, they forgot that I am like a banyan tree, whose roots are stronger than its branches, and that's why we are coming to Rise & Fall to stir things up).” Sharing his plans for his time in the Tower, he added, “Waha ke Penthouse pe kabza nahi karenge darbaar lagayenge aur raj karenge neeche wala Basement ke logowa ke upar. (I won't just occupy the penthouse there; we'll run a darbaar and rule over the people in the basement)". “Aur duniya ko batla dijiye humara parivaar pura Bihar hai. (And tell the world that the entire Bihar is our family)," Tej Pratap ended up declaring. Meanwhile, former Indian cricketer Virender Sehwag will be making his OTT debut as the host of "Rise and Fall Season 2". “Cricket has taught me one thing—no match is won before the final ball, and Rise and Fall Season 2 takes that unpredictability to another level. As a host, what excites me about this game is that there are no easy wins and no fixed positions,” he shared. "Rise & Fall Season 2" will premiere on 26th September and air every day at 12 PM, for free on Prime Video and the MX Player Android app. --IANS pm/

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM launches national innovation challenge, flags off car rally - Punjab Kesari English
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM launches national innovation challenge, flags off car rally By: IANS On: Saturday, September 19, 2026 8:00 PM Google News Follow Us Patna, Sep 19 (IANS) Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday inaugurated the National Innovation Challenge, organised as part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan (Service Pledge Campaign), by lighting a ceremonial lamp at Ramandal. He also launched the National Innovation Challenge portal. At the beginning of the programme, Choudhary flagged off 25 vehicles participating in the Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Car Rally. He later visited the innovation exhibition, inspected various stalls, and interacted with young entrepreneurs to learn about their startup innovations, products, and technologies. Addressing the gathering, Choudhary welcomed participants and said the spirit of service must be accompanied by a collective resolve to build a Viksit Bharat (Developed India) by 2047. He congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years in public service, adding that PM Modi’s vision and emphasis on innovation continue to inspire the country. Choudhary said the state government was working towards these objectives, with service, innovation, technology, and entrepreneurship playing an important role in Bihar’s development. He emphasised that the state’s large youth population and workforce should be viewed as an asset and transformed into a driving force for development rather than a challenge. He said initiatives such as the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan and the Seva First Innovation Challenge (East Zone) were encouraging young people to embrace service, innovation, and new ideas. The Chief Minister highlighted that technology was being used to simplify citizens’ lives. The government had transferred financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of nine lakh flood-affected families. He added that the government stood firmly with families affected by disasters and was making every possible effort to support them. Highlighting Bihar’s digital transformation, Choudhary said UPI had revolutionised digital transactions and noted its widespread use in India. He said Bihar had created a conducive environment for industrial investment, with land already allocated to around 1,000 industrial units. The government has set a target of establishing 10,000 industries in Bihar over the next five years. Referring to migration for employment, Choudhary said around 12 lakh people from Bihar currently migrate to other states for wage-based work. The government’s objective, he said, was to create sufficient employment opportunities within Bihar so that people would not have to leave the state. The Chief Minister said young entrepreneurs could play a significant role in transforming Bihar’s development trajectory through startups and assured them of government support. He also highlighted initiatives to promote innovation in the information technology sector through the Bihar Tech Portal for Innovation in the IT Sector. Choudhary said the government was accelerating work in education. He said the government had established 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan model schools. Through the Vidyarthi Sathi app, students have access to live classes and preparation facilities for competitive examinations such as NEET and JEE. bihar_raw_news.content: Maha govt indifferent amid severe drought: Congress By: IANS On: Saturday, September 19, 2026 8:00 PM Google News Follow Us Mumbai, Sep 19 (IANS) Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC) President Harshwardhan Sapkal on Saturday demanded that the government immediately declare a drought, credit Rs 50,000 per hectare directly into farmers’ bank accounts, and grant a blanket loan waiver. He warned that if these measures are not taken promptly, ministers will face public backlash and will not be permitted to move freely across the state. Sapkal told reporters that a severe drought situation prevails in several parts of Maharashtra, with no rainfall recorded for over a month and a half, causing standing crops to wither completely. He alleged that the BJP-led Mahayuti government remains indifferent to the crisis. While discussions take place during cabinet meetings, no concrete decisions have been made, and guardian ministers have failed to visit affected farmers. “The government spends Rs 350 crore on CCTV installations for the Kumbh Mela, yet hesitates to release funds for farmers. Despite the desperate need, no decision was made to attempt cloud seeding,” he said. Sapkal said public anger against the ruling coalition is at an all-time high, accusing the administration of caring only about corruption and commissions rather than citizens’ welfare. He urged the government to act before the festive season and disburse aid before Dasara. He sharply criticised the call to light lamps on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, questioning the administration’s performance over the past 12 years. He pointed out that youth remain unemployed, women’s safety is compromised, farmers face ruin, the economy has deteriorated, and inflation continues to surge. “Celebrating birthdays while citizens are suffering in crisis is uncalled for,” Sapkal said. He highlighted the hypocrisy of PM Modi previously urging the public to practice austerity, such as reducing oil consumption, limiting foreign travel, and avoiding gold purchases, while now asking people to light oil lamps for his birthday. He termed this an act of self-glorification and criticised the leadership for misleading the public. The MPCC chief further accused the Election Commission of India of functioning as a tool for the ruling BJP. He asserted that implementing SIR threatens democracy by attempting to strip citizens of their right to vote. Sapkal said the Commission’s functioning is leading toward lawlessness, adding that the Congress Party will firmly oppose these moves and continue to fight on the streets to protect democracy in the country. –IANS sj/dan (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. bihar_raw_news.title: BSEB To Construct 29 Hi-Tech Examination Buildings In Bihar At ₹330.07 Crore
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) will construct 29 hi-tech examination building-cum-strong rooms at 29 locations across 27 districts of Bihar at an estimated cost of ₹330.07 crore. The project has received administrative approval, with the buildings planned as dedicated centres for conducting examinations and handling confidential examination material. #Bihar #BSEB #BiharBoard @BiharEducation_ @mkrtiwari_bjp @samrat4bjp pic.twitter.com/ReYJ68A2Fn — Bihar School Examination Board (@officialbseb) September 19, 2026 The proposed G+3 examination buildings will be constructed on around 1 to 1.5 acres of land at each location. According to BSEB, each building will have the capacity to accommodate around 4,000 candidates simultaneously across three examination halls, with CCTV surveillance. Examination centres to reduce dependence on Schools, Colleges The new facilities are intended to reduce the use of schools and colleges as examination centres for various state-level examinations. BSEB said examinations conducted by different commissions, departments and other agencies at the district level often affect regular teaching and internal examinations in educational institutions. The dedicated examination buildings are expected to allow schools and colleges to continue their academic activities without disruption when examinations are being conducted in the district. The centres will also be located at prominent institutions near district headquarters to make it easier for candidates to reach examination venues, BSEB said. Facilities for answer sheet storage & evaluation The examination buildings will serve multiple purposes beyond conducting exams. The halls can be used for storing answer sheets after examinations and as evaluation centres for checking answer sheets. The strong rooms will be used to store confidential examination material. The facilities will also support the barcoding and scanning of answer sheets whenever required. BSEB said the buildings could also be used for election-related activities, helping ensure that regular teaching and learning in schools and other educational institutions are not affected during elections. 24x7 CCTV Monitoring, Fire Safety Systems The proposed buildings will be equipped with several security and safety features, including fire alarms, firefighting equipment and disaster management systems. CCTV cameras will provide 24x7 monitoring and recording of activities at the centres. The examination building-cum-strong rooms will eventually be handed over to the schools or colleges where they are constructed for operation and maintenance. BSEB and the concerned educational institution will share the revenue generated through the use of the facilities. The project is aimed at creating permanent, multipurpose examination infrastructure that can be used for board examinations, competitive examinations, evaluation work and the secure handling of confidential examination material.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela this afternoon through video conferencing. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi emphasized the pivotal role of youth in building a developed and self-reliant India. He said that in recent years, the Central government has consistently focused on equipping the youth with the skills and opportunities needed to prepare for the future. Prime Minister Modi said the government is also working to rapidly expand employment opportunities in the private sector. He said, with this objective, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched with an outlay of around one lakh crore. The scheme is expected to enable nearly two crore young people to enter the workforce for the first time. Prime Minister Modi said that India has signed Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries in the past few years, which is opening new doors of opportunity for the country’s youth. He said, such trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for country’s entrepreneurs, and create new career possibilities for the youth. Prime Minister Modi said that India is today the world’s third largest startup ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: 44 mins ago | National 71 Nepalese Finance Minister Wagle Calls for Renewed India-Nepal Partnership
national_raw_news.content: Nepalese Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle has stated that India and Nepal have an opportunity to renew their partnership by building on the strong ties that already exist. Addressing an International Seminar on ‘Reimagining India-Nepal Relations in an Emerging Global Order’ organized by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) in New Delhi today, Dr Wagle emphasised the importance of strengthening connectivity and economic cooperation and realising the considerable potential that the two countries can achieve together. Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, the Nepalese Finance Minister also stressed upon urgent pre-disaster investments, including early warning systems and resilient infrastructure, to mitigate climate risks. On energy cooperation and cross-border electricity trade, Dr Wagle highlighted ongoing joint projects supported by Indian investments. Dr Wagle also commended India’s prompt relief and rescue assistance following recent flash floods in Nepal. He further informed that Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah is expected to visit India by the end of this year. Additional Secretary (North) at the Ministry of External Affairs, Munu Mahawar, also highlighted the need for greater ambition in taking forward the India-Nepal partnership. He noted that the two countries have made significant progress in areas such as connectivity and power, while emphasising the opportunity to advance more ambitious projects and initiatives that have remained unrealised for decades. He underlined that the potential of the relationship is much larger and therefore calls for greater ambition in goal-setting. In his welcome address, Director General of RIS, Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma highlighted the strong complementarities that exist between India and Nepal across trade, energy, education, health and development cooperation. He emphasised the need to deepen engagement so that the relationship can move from proximity to prosperity and ultimately towards shared prosperity.

national_raw_news.title: 47 mins ago | Sports 69 20th Asian Games Officially Opened at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan
national_raw_news.content: The 20th Asian Games officially got underway today at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan, with Emperor Naruhito declaring the Games open. The two-hour ceremony was attended by Japan’s royal family, Games officials, and Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani. India’s 501-member contingent was led by double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat during the athletes’ parade. Sehrawat replaced shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor as flag-bearer after the latter did not receive his ceremonial kit on time. Some events have already begun, including women’s cricket, where India have already advanced to the semifinals after an eight-wicket win over Japan yesterday. India will face Bangladesh in the second semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, tomorrow. In Teqball, which is making its Asian Games debut, India’s Quimcy D’Souza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles semifinal and will play Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto for bronze medal tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his best wishes to the Indian contingent as the Asian Games commenced today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. In his message, Mr Modi said each athlete has worked incredibly hard and shown remarkable dedication and determination and India is proud of them. He hoped that the athletes play well and shine at the Games.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi Government Approves Notification of 1,000 Acres in Southern Ridge as Reserved Forest 15 mins ago 8
national_raw_news.content: Delhi government has approved the notification of around 1,000 acres of additional land in the Southern Ridge as Reserved Forest. With this decision, the notified Ridge area will increase to around 13,000 acres. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that the decision has been taken under Section 20 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927. She added that the Delhi Ridge is not only a part of the capital’s natural heritage but also its green protective shield. Ms Gupta also said that the government’s aim is to ensure the protection, scientific restoration and revival of the Delhi Ridge so that this natural area remains protected for future generations as well. Ms Gupta further added that providing legal protection to the land is not the government’s only objective but reviving the Ridge’s ecosystem is equally important. With this objective, scientific ecological restoration is being taken forward in accordance with the Ridge Working Plan. She informed that special emphasis is being placed on promoting native species, restoring degraded areas and scientifically managing invasive species. The Delhi Ridge Management Board was also constituted this year for the conservation, restoration and management of the Delhi Ridge. Its responsibilities include protecting the Ridge, scientific ecological restoration, afforestation and habitat conservation.

national_raw_news.title: Two-day Northeast Education Conclave 2026 concludes in Nagaland 54 mins ago 19
national_raw_news.content: The two-day Northeast Education Conclave 2026 concluded today at Naga United Village, Chümoukedima, in Nagaland bringing together policymakers, educators and administrators from across the Northeast to deliberate on the implementation of the National Education Policy, NEP 2020. The conclave was organised by the Government of Nagaland in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Government of India, on the theme, “Implementation of NEP 2020: Vision, Challenges & Opportunities for the North Eastern States.” Speaking at the valedictory ceremony today Tripura Minister for Higher Education, Panchayats and General Administration, Kishor Barman, called for effective implementation of NEP 2020 to make education more skill-oriented and future-ready in the Northeast. Mr Barman said over Rs 21,000 crore has been invested in the education sector in the Northeast over the past decade, along with the establishment of around 850 schools, nine medical colleges, two IIITs and nearly 200 skill development institutions. He stressed the need to strengthen internships, apprenticeships, skill-based courses, entrepreneurship and career counselling, and called for greater regional collaboration in research and student mobility. Mr Barman also urged the Northeast to transform brain drain into brain circulation. Additional Secretary, Department of Education, Ministry of Education, Anandrao V. Patel, stressed the need to make education more multidisciplinary and skill-oriented, and to strengthen its links with industry. Mr Patel highlighted the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme, saying industries can provide apprenticeship and employment opportunities to students from the Northeast. He said companies are already recruiting students from the region, including through apprenticeship programmes, and urged the states to further strengthen industry-academia linkages. Mr Patel also called for reducing dropouts and achieving a 50 percent Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education by 2035, stressing the greater use of digital education and technology. The conclave proposed key outcomes and resolutions, including infrastructure upgrades through the establishment of Skill Hubs in parent institutions, vertical mobility and academic progression, promotion of the North-East Knowledge System and Indigenous Knowledge institutions; establishment of State Public Universities, annual education review meetings and conclaves, and a special financial package for NEP 2020 implementation. The conclave also proposed that a dedicated Prime Minister’s Special Financial Package for the North-Eastern States may be considered to support the effective implementation of NEP 2020 in the region.
